claim: bde bar gshegs pa = Sanskrit Tathagata
evidence: Sugata is bde bar gshegs pa ('gone to bliss'); Tathagata is de bzhin gshegs pa.

claim: Mother of Mrigara = famous female lay disciple Vishakha
evidence: Visakha was nicknamed Migaramata, 'Migara's mother', chief female lay disciple.

claim: bampo (bam po) = section/portion
evidence: No source checked; bam po conventionally a text division, but not verified.

claim: 'three circles' likely = kingship, subjects, neighbors
evidence: No source found for this reading.

claim: Namgru is likely a phonetic rendering of a Sanskrit name
evidence: Nam gru ('boat of the heaven') is the Tibetan translation of Revati (a lunar mansion); the Brahmin Raivata is rendered nam gru, i.e. a semantic translation, not phonetic. Sanskrit name is Raivata (Lalitavistara).
correction: Right that the underlying name is Sanskrit (Raivata), but the Tibetan is a translation of Revati/Raivata rather than a phonetic rendering.

claim: Text is the Hundred Syllable Mantra of Vajrasattva
evidence: Mantra 'oṃ vajrasattva samayam anupālaya vajrasattva tvenopatiṣṭha dṛḍho me bhava...' is the Hundred Syllable Mantra of Vajrasattva.

claim: phyi stong pa nyid = bahirdhā-śūnyatā
evidence: Outer emptiness (bahirdhāśūnyatā, Tibetan phyi stong pa nyid), per Madhyamakavatara listing.

claim: gzugs med pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa = ārūpyasamāpatti
evidence: gzugs med pa'i snyoms par 'jug pa corresponds to ārūpyasamāpatti, formless absorptions.

claim: Detailed Play (Rgya cher rol pa) = Lalitavistara Sutra
evidence: Lalitavistara's Tibetan title is 'phags pa rgya cher rol pa; 84000 'The Play in Full'.

claim: bzod pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa = kṣānti-pāramitā
evidence: Entry: bzod pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa = perfection of patience, kṣāntipāramitā.

claim: Blo gros brtan pa = Sthiramati
evidence: Blo gros brtan pa can be Sthiramati (6th c. scholar), but in the Śūraṃgamasamādhi sūtra the interlocutor Blo gros brtan pa is the bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati (Toh 132).
correction: Sanskrit should be Dṛḍhamati, not Sthiramati (name equivalence is for the 6th-c. scholar).

claim: Phonetic renderings of Sanskrit dharanis
Marpa and Ngok = Marpa Lotsawa and his disciple Ngok Choku Dorje
evidence: Ngok Chöku Dorje (1036-1097/1102) was a close disciple of Marpa; the Ngok lineage Marpa Kagyu (rigpawiki.org Ngok Chöku Dorje).

claim: description of chant style
Opening is Sanskrit transliterated into Tibetan
ngo bo nyid stong pa nyid = prakṛti-śūnyatā
evidence: ngo bo nyid stong pa nyid is svabhāvaśūnyatā; prakṛtiśūnyatā is rang bzhin stong pa nyid.

claim: phonetic transcription of Sanskrit mantras
Sharadvatiputra = another name for Shariputra
evidence: Śāradvatīputra is an alternate/full form of Śāriputra.

claim: Sanskrit vowels and consonants for mantra purification
Passage is a Sanskrit dharani invoking Great Compassionate One, Great Lotus-Handed One, Great Pure Being
evidence: This is the Avalokiteshvara Mahākaruṇika dhāraṇī; mahākāruṇika = greatly compassionate (padma-hasta = lotus-hand, literal).

claim: note fragment about medicine
note is passage text
